investigation.headline: This rejection appears correct

checks.title: Specified disease waiting period
checks.finding: Knee replacement for osteoarthritis that was not caused by an accident is on the policy's 24-month waiting list, and the policy had been held for only 6 months, so the waiting period was not over.
checks.policy_quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed conditions, surgeries or treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of Continuous Coverage after the date of inception of the first policy.

checks.title: Claims Review Committee approval
checks.finding: The letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the rejection on 01-Oct-2026.
checks.policy_quote: No claim shall be repudiated, fully or partly, without the approval of the Company's Claims Review Committee (a three-member committee).
checks.regulation: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance, 2024

checks.title: Specific clause cited
checks.finding: The letter names the exact clause used to reject the claim: Clause 3.2 — Excl02, the 24-month waiting period.
checks.policy_quote: Every repudiation letter shall state the specific clause of the Policy under which the claim is declined, and inform the Insured Person of the grievance redressal and Ombudsman options.

checks.title: Moratorium period (60 months)

next_steps: Accept that this claim is unlikely to succeed: knee replacement has a 24-month waiting period, and your policy was only 6 months old.

Keep renewing on time (within the 30-day grace period). The 24-month wait counts from 01-Mar-2026, so knee replacement cover should start after 28-Feb-2028. Your hospital notes mention 3 years of knee pain, so the insurer may argue the condition existed before the policy, which carries a 36-month wait. Plan for a possible wait until 01-Mar-2029.
For the other knee, or if surgery is needed sooner, check whether you or your spouse have employer group health cover, which often has no waiting period.
If you had any earlier health policy without a break in cover, ask the insurer in writing for portability credit, as this could shorten the waiting period.
